records.name: Jogailė
records.facts_used: Antanas Pakerys studies Jogailė among Lithuanian two-stem feminine names, which he describes as usually formed after the corresponding masculine names. Its masculine counterpart is Jogaila, the name of the fourteenth-century grand duke. Antanas Salys called the first element hitherto unexplained, tentatively linking it with riding, and connected gail- with gailas “fierce, vehement”; these are scholarly proposals, not a settled translation. In his 2011 article Pakerys cites Lithuanian population-register data showing Jogailė among the most popular two-stem girls’ names: 164 girls born in 1999–2010 had it. This is a dated record of modern use; it does not date the name’s first appearance.
records.reason: Exact-form evidence supports a reviewed history in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Checked location: Pakerys 2011, PDF 1 / printed 90 (compound feminine names usually formed after masculine names) and PDF 2 / printed 91, visually checked: Jogailė (164) among popular two-stem girls’ names, 1999–2010 register data. Salys 1983, Jogaila article (reprint of Lietuvių Enciklopedija IX), PDF 90–91 / printed 75–76, visually checked: first element “iki šiol neišaiškintas”, tentatively *jot(i)- / jóti; gail- with gailas. Salys’s stem list PDF 289 / printed 274 instead says “Jo- : plg. jau”, so the first element is explicitly kept uncertain.
